newsitem.title: USA: Oncor process for prostate test promising.
newsitem.headline: Oncor process for prostate test promising.

text.p: Oncor Inc said Wednesday that preliminary study findings support the use of HER-2/neu gene amplification as a molecular marker in the evaluation of patients with prostate cancer.
HER-2/neu gene amplification is a process in which a cell sample is removed from the affected area of the patient, coated with a substance and then magnified for study.

Oncor said the results, which has been published in the current issue of Cancer, the journal of the American Cancer Society, demonstrated that HER-2/neu gene amplification significantly correlated with tumor grade and DNA ploidy status and was more sensitive than the antibody method in detecting HER-2/neu gene abnormalities.

Oncor said it intends to develop clinical uses for HER-2/neu gene amplification by conducting clinical trials and obtaining regulatory approvals for diagnostic and prognostic assays or prognostic assays alone.
A patent application has been filed for the use of technology to detect HER-2/neu gene amplification associated with prostate cancer.
Oncor said its INFORM HER-2/neu breast cancer test is under review by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
